August 2, 1940.

Deputy Commissioner in Charge.

Indian Publicity Sub-Committee.

With reference to the report on the above subject dated
July 26th, 1940, the five resolutions adopted are worthy of further
comment.

1. The question arises as to what method will be adopted for
the translation daily of the Noon News Bulletin. The suggestion
put forward that it be done through this office is not feasible
for very obvious reasons.

2. The Indian Government policy regarding religion is "Strict
Neutrality" and the use of the Gurdwara and Mosques for the
dissemination of propaganda is not advisable.

3. This office cannot undertake the distribution of propaganda
with Police Orders as it will be a sign of weakness on our part.
If it is known that agitation is rife amongst the Sikh Police it
requires sterner methods than propaganda leaflets.

4. The answer to this is similar to No. 1.

5. The idea is good but all necessary arrangements and
distribution of tickets etc. should be undertaken by an outside
source.

On the 21st December 1939 this office was asked by
Mr. A.A.L. Tuson of the British Embassy for suggestions regarding
the dissemination of propaganda amongst the local Sikh Community
and a copy of the reply forwarded is attached. I am still of
opinion that propaganda coming from India would have greater
results than anything that could be done locally.

DC SP Br.
Agree.
The Police cannot undertake
this work.

（签名）
Deputy Commissioner (Sikhs).

关于1940年7月26日就上述主题提交的报告，
所通过的五项决议值得进一步评论。

1. 问题在于将采取何种方法每日翻译《午间新闻简报》。
有人建议通过本办公室进行翻译，但出于显而易见的原因，
此建议不可行。

2. 印度政府在宗教方面的政策是“严格中立”，
利用谒师堂（Gurdwara）和清真寺传播宣传品是不妥当的。

3. 本办公室不能随同警务命令分发宣传品，
因为这将被视为我方软弱的表现。如果得知锡克警员中
煽动情绪盛行，则需要比宣传传单更强硬的手段。

4. 对此的回答与第1点类似。

5. 这个想法很好，但所有必要的安排以及
门票分发等工作应由外部来源承担。

1939年12月21日，英国大使馆的A.A.L. Tuson先生

Dear .r. .uson,

In reply to your letter of December 21st, 1930 re the
subject of publicity of Indian information to the local Indian
Community.

At present this office distributes the following Indian
newspapers to the members of the Sikh Branch at the Council's
expense.

1. Fouji Akhbar (Army paper) in Gurmukhi - 1 copy weekly.
2. Khalsa Samachar (Sikh Affairs) " " -16 copies "
3. Sher-i-Punjab (Lion of the Punjab in Urdu-12 " "

I would, therefore, suggest the following:-

a) Continue the Fouji Akhbar as at present.
b) Increase the issue of the Khalsa Samachar to 100 copies per week.
c Increase the issue of the Sher-i-Punjab to 70 copies per week.
d) Order 40 copies per week of the "Zimindar" a paper purely for
the Mohammedan Community.

If you are prepared to meet the additional expense of the
extra copies, I would propose that after the insertion of the
propaganda in India, they be posted to us in the usual way and the
distribution would be carried out by this office in the usual way
so as not to arouse any suspicion.

The following information about the above three papers
should be carefully noted.

1. Fouji Akhbar. This is purely an Army newspaper and only
deals with promotions, transfers, troop movements etc. Apart from
this information there is little to interest the men. The original
idea of the paper was to keep our men in touch with the doings of
their regiments as a big proportion of them were ex-soldiers. It
would serve for both the Sikh and the Mohammedan Communities but
for the fact that it is printed in Gurmukhi, the language of the
Sikhs.
page_data.zh:
亲爱的 .r. .uson，

回复您1930年12月21日关于向当地印度社群
发布印度信息宣传事宜的来信。

目前，本办公室由公董局出资，向锡克分队的成员
分发以下印度报纸。

1. 《Fouji Akhbar》（军队报纸），古木基文（Gurmukhi）版 - 每周1份。
2. 《Khalsa Samachar》（锡克事务） " " - 每周16份
3. 《Sher-i-Punjab》（旁遮普之狮），乌尔都语版 - 每周12份 " "

因此，我建议如下：-

a) 继续按现状发行《Fouji Akhbar》。
b) 将《Khalsa Samachar》的发行量增加至每周100份。
c) 将《Sher-i-Punjab》的发行量增加至每周70份。
d) 每周订购40份《Zimindar》，这是一份纯粹面向
穆斯林社群的报纸。

如果您愿意承担额外份数的费用，我建议在印度插入
宣传内容后，按常规方式邮寄给我们，并由本办公室
按常规方式进行分发，以免引起任何怀疑。

应仔细注意有关上述三份报纸的以下信息。

1. 《Fouji Akhbar》。这纯粹是一份军队报纸，仅涉及
晋升、调动、部队移动等。除了这些信息外，
几乎没有其他能引起士兵兴趣的内容。创办该报的初衷
是让我们的士兵与其所属团体的动态保持联系，因为其中
很大一部分人是退伍军人。如果不是因为它用锡克人的语言
古木基文印刷，它本可以服务于锡克和穆斯林两个社群。

2. □□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□

3. Sher-i-Punjab or Lion of the Punjab. This publication is also pro-Sikh but does not touch on religion. Although printed in India I do not consider it a suitable paper for the Mohammedan Community. It has on occasions had a definite anti-British outlook.

For any effective propaganda amongst the local community it is the opinion of this office that the only feasible method would be to have pamphlets or an extra page inserted in these papers in India before despatching them to Shanghai. The only means available to us for this type of work is the laborious method of writing it out by hand and the copies turned out by a Duplicator. This, though possible, would not create a good impression on the Indians, but on the contrary might be construed as a sign of weakness both on the part of this office and the British Consulate.

Lastly, I would suggest that this office be supplied with a copy of articles of "Indian Information", articles considered useful we could disseminate by word of mouth.

A few articles have from time to time appeared in the English press such as Mohammedan troops sent to France, or speeches of loyalty by some Indian Princes who incidentally have also been of the Mohammedan faith. This type of news would not create a favourable impression in the minds of Sikhs who form the greater percentage of the community.

(Sd) W. E. Fairbairn.
Assistant Commissioner (Sikhs).

2. □□□…

3. 《旁遮普之狮》（Sher-i-Punjab or Lion of the Punjab）。该出版物亦持亲锡克教立场，但不涉及宗教议题。尽管在印度印刷，本处认为其并不适合作为面向穆斯林社区的刊物。该刊偶尔表现出明确的反英倾向。

就针对本地社区开展有效宣传而言，本处认为，唯一可行的办法是在这些刊物发往上海之前，于印度境内插入小册子或增页。我们为此类工作所能采用的唯一手段，是费时费力的手工抄写，并使用油印机复制副本。此举虽属可行，但不会给印度人留下良好印象，反而可能被解读为本处及英国领事馆示弱的迹象。

最后，我建议向本处提供一份《印度情报》（Indian Information）的文章副本；对于被认为有用的文章，我们可以通过口头方式加以传播。

英文报刊上不时刊登一些文章，例如派遣穆斯林部队前往法国，或某些印度王公发表效忠演说（这些王公碰巧也信奉穆斯林信仰）。此类新闻不会在构成社区大多数的锡克教徒心中留下有利印象。

（签名）W. E. Fairbairn
助理总监（锡克教事务）

Minutes of the first meeting of the Indian Sub-Committee of the British
Publicity Committee held in the offices of the British & Chinese
Corporation Limited, 27, The Bund, at 4.0 p.m. on Thursday, July 25th 1940.

The following gentlemen were present:

Mr.F.D.Bhedwar, representing B.L.Tata & CO.Ltd.

3. The Chairman defined the aims of the Committee as follows:
Firstly, the countering of subversive activities amongst the Indian
community; secondly, the finding of ways in which a true and factual
picture of what is taking place in the world to-day can be conveyed to
the Indian community, with special reference to its less educated members
who are unable to read or understand English.

The Chairman expressed his conviction that such a representative
committee could continue to serve a most useful purpose, even after the
end of the war, for the discussion of problems and matters of common
concern.

4. Various methods of publicity and information were then discussed.
It was decided that a daily news bulletin in Gurmukhi, cheaply printed
on a duplicating machine and distributed at certain points, would be a
most valuable means of reaching the large Sikh community, for whom no
provision at the moment is made at all in the provision of news.

Mr. Purja Singh and Mr. Stewart Young undertook to get in touch with
Mr. Robertson, Deputy Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, since
Mr. Robertson already supervises the issue of the police orders in
Gurmukhi and it was felt that use might possibly be made of his translator
and duplicating machine. Arrangements similar to the above might also
be made as regards the needs of the less educated Indians.

5. As regards broadcasting, the first requisite was three or more
receiving sets to be placed in the Gurdwara and elsewhere where the Sikhs
and Moslems meet every Friday and Sunday respectively. Mr. Moorhead
undertook to secure these. Soon it is hoped to arrange news broadcasts
and addresses by prominent Indian residents over the local radio station
X.G.H.

6. As regards the dissemination of information by other means it was
decided that ways must be devised of conveying news direct to those
Indians who are not members of the various religious communities. The

3. 主席将委员会的目标界定如下：
第一， counter（对抗）印度社群中的颠覆活动；第二，寻找途径，向印度社群传达当今世界局势的真实且符合事实的图景，特别针对其受教育程度较低、无法阅读或理解英语的成员。

主席表示坚信，这样一个具有代表性的委员会即使在战争结束后，仍可在讨论共同关心的问题及事项方面继续发挥极有益的作用。

4. 随后讨论了各种宣传和信息传播方法。会议决定，用古木基文（Gurmukhi）编写每日新闻简报，通过油印机廉价印刷并在特定地点分发，将是接触广大锡克教社群的最有价值的手段，目前该社群在新闻供给方面完全没有任何安排。

普尔贾·辛格先生（Mr. Purja Singh）和斯图尔特·扬先生（Mr. Stewart Young）负责与上海公共租界工部局警务处副总监罗伯逊先生（Mr. Robertson）取得联系，因为罗伯逊先生已经监管古木基文警务命令的发布工作，大家认为或许可以利用他的翻译人员和油印机。对于受教育程度较低的印度人的需求，也可以作出类似的安排。

5. 关于广播方面，首要条件是在锡克教谒师所（Gurdwara）以及锡克教徒和穆斯林分别于每周五和周日聚会的其他地方，放置三台或更多的收音接收机。穆尔黑德先生（Mr. Moorhead）承诺负责获取这些设备。不久后，希望能安排通过本地广播电台 X.G.H. 播放新闻广播以及由知名印度居民发表的演讲。

6. 关于通过其他手段传播信息，会议决定必须设法将新闻直接传达给那些不属于各个宗教团体的印度人。

7. The Committee decided that a drive should be made to increase the
Indian membership of the British Residents Association and to see whether
special provision could not be made for those poorer members of the Indian
community who are unable to contribute the full subscription.

Mr. Morrison undertook to get in touch with the Secretary of the
B.R.A. and to provide the members of the Committee with membership lists
and entrance forms.

8. After the Committee had discussed these several points they were
joined by Mr. John Alexander, Press Attaché of the British Embassy and
accordingly representative in Shanghai of the Ministry of Information.
Mr. Alexander was introduced by Mr. Bodha to the members of the Committee
and was informed briefly of the results of the Committee's deliberations.
He expressed his great appreciation of the formation of the group, and
his warm approval of its aims and objectives. He hoped that the Chairman
would consent, as representative of the group, to join the large advisory
Publicity Committee.

9. The Committee finally broke up after having decided that a further
meeting should be held in a week's time, namely, on Thursday, August 1st,
at 4.30 p.m. in the offices of the British and Chinese Corporation.

Comment on the copies of the bulletins
covering the week ending November 24th, as well
as the weekly edition is distinctly favourable.

Indians are anxious to listen in but few possess radio
